title: Switch block in a DIP case
pinRule: lever k joins pin k and pin 2n+1-k: pins 1..n down one side, n+1..2n back up the other, so lever 1 is pins 1 and 2n
values: lever count is in the type: SW-DIP-4
datasheet: none found yet; the pin rule above is the usual layout, not read from a datasheet
note: The usual DIP switch layout; the real part on a board is not checked against a datasheet. The sheet's switches section (same ref) gives what each lever means; the two must agree (checked when a sheet is read).
